title: Maximum Favorable Excursion (MFE)
summary: MFE is the greatest favorable movement reached while a position was open. It is useful for reviewing trade management, but it is hindsight information and does not prove that the trader could or should have exited at the maximum.

title: Maximum Adverse Excursion (MAE)
summary: MAE is the greatest adverse movement reached while a position was open. It helps review entry quality, stop placement, and how much adverse movement a setup typically experiences before resolution.

title: High of Day (HOD)
summary: HOD is the highest traded price reached so far during the defined trading session. It is dynamic: a new higher print creates a new HOD. It is a reference level, not an automatic entry signal.

title: Low of Day (LOD)
summary: LOD is the lowest traded price reached so far during the defined trading session. It updates when a new session low prints and should be interpreted with structure, participation, and context.

title: Premarket High (PMH)
summary: PMH is the highest traded price reached during the defined premarket session. Thin liquidity or isolated prints can make a level less informative, so context matters.

title: Premarket Low (PML)
summary: PML is the lowest traded price reached during the defined premarket session. Treat it as a reference area that still requires confirmation and context.

title: Prior-Day High (PDH)
summary: PDH is the previous trading day’s high. It can act as a widely visible reference, but a break matters only when price behavior, liquidity, volume, and acceptance support the interpretation.

title: Prior-Day Low (PDL)
summary: PDL is the previous trading day’s low. It provides higher-timeframe location but should not be treated as a guaranteed support or reversal price.

title: Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP)
summary: VWAP is an intraday average price weighted by volume. Traders use it as one piece of location and participation context; VWAP alone is not a complete trade signal.

title: Exponential Moving Average (EMA)
summary: An EMA is a moving average that gives more weight to recent prices. It can help visualize trend and price relationship, but it lags price and should be combined with structure and context.

title: Average True Range (ATR)
summary: ATR measures historical price-range volatility over a chosen lookback. It describes magnitude, not direction, and its value changes with settings and timeframe.

title: R and R-Multiple
summary: R is a standardized unit of initial planned risk. A result of +2R means the result was twice the initial planned risk; -1R means a loss equal to that risk unit.

title: Reason for Entry
summary: The reason for entry is the evidence-based explanation for why a trade is permitted at that moment. It is different from the broader thesis and from the specific trigger that authorizes execution.

title: Entry Trigger
summary: An entry trigger is the specific observable event that must occur before the planned entry is allowed. It converts a general trade thesis into an executable rule.

title: Invalidation
summary: Invalidation is the evidence that makes the original trade premise no longer valid. It should be defined before entry so decisions are not rewritten after P&L changes.

title: Reason for Exit
summary: The actual reason for exit records why the position was closed. It should be compared with the planned exit logic to separate plan execution from emotional or unplanned decisions.

title: Higher High / Higher Low
summary: Higher highs and higher lows are observations about swing structure. A sequence of them can support an uptrend interpretation, but confirmation rules and timeframe matter.

title: Lower High / Lower Low
summary: Lower highs and lower lows are observations about swing structure. They can support a downtrend interpretation when confirmed on the relevant timeframe.

title: NO TRADE Decision
summary: NO TRADE is a valid decision when required evidence, liquidity, risk, or confirmation is missing. Good process includes recognizing when not to enter, not only finding entries.

title: Plan Versus Actual
summary: Plan Versus Actual compares what was defined before entry with what actually happened. The goal is to distinguish outcome from process and identify where execution diverged from the original plan.

title: MFE Capture %
summary: MFE Capture % compares realized favorable P&L with the maximum favorable excursion observed while the position was open. It is a review metric, not a universal score of exit quality.

title: Paper-to-Live Transfer Gap
summary: The paper-to-live transfer gap compares decision behavior in simulation with behavior when real money is involved. Differences in plan adherence, MAE, exit timing, or mistakes can reveal where execution changes under pressure.
